posts.cooked:
Ok, just got my pre-order of WotC, and was looking at the Wager Master Enemy Deck.

I saw the card "Breaking the Rules".

It is a ongoing card that states:

"The phases of Heo turns now go in nthe following order:

   End of Turn

   Draw a Card

   Use a Power

   Play a Card

   Start of Turn"

I am confused about how this affects the game. Does this mean that the players turn starts then passes to the next player, whose turn doesn't start until after the draw/power/play phases? This seems to me to be a card that will lock down the heros and hand the game to the villain. What am I missing here?

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
coconaught:

But this card helps a lot of heroes including wager masters nemesis Guise.  With all the ongoings in his deck and others that destroy themselves at the start of the turn, they can now stay in effect until they are done destroying the villains with them.  Not to mention the whole drawing before you do anything else adds a little more strategy to things.  I think it is kind of a fun concept.

They still have a Start of Turn phase while Breaking the Rules is in play, it is located after the Play Phase. So if Guise plays one of his ongoings while Breaking the Rules is in play, that card will be destroyed on the very next phase. So it actually makes it a lot more difficult to play as Guise, as he can't use his Ongoings without out of turn plays and/or Fixed Point.

posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
It works if you time it right.  If you play the ongoings the turn before Breaking the Rules comes into play, and then destory it with Retcon when your turn rolls around, you can skip the start of turn for one turn, and get double use out of his stuff.

 

That said, if Breaking the Rules comes out at the wrong time and you can't get rid of it, it will really ruin your day.

 

And if you can get Into the Stratosphere to be played on Guise's turn (which is tricky, but possible), then you could potentially net 3 rounds of use.
